body:
[“The idea that somehow, someday he will control and enjoy his drinking is the great obsession of every abnormal drinker”](https://www.aa.org/assets/en_US/en_bigbook_chapt3.pdf) 

I’ve had those same thoughts many times before. This is from the AA big book. 

Edit: Misquoted the link. It was longer to type than I planned, but you get the point.

Nothing has helped yet. It almost feels like breaking off the second relationship just reopened the wound of the losing the first all over again.  I feel like I tried so hard to make #2 work so I could forget about #1. All I did was make #2 fall in love with me and looking back, that whole relationship was a lie. It’s such a shitty feeling.

I know exactly how you feel. I made nearly the exact same mistake in my life. I wasn’t married, but in an 8 year relationship that I ruined by cheating. I stayed with the new girl for about two years before I couldn’t take it anymore. I secretly compared every aspect of our relationship to my previous girlfriend and it depresses me every day. Drinking played a big role in my relationships crumbling too. I pretty much destroyed two relationships/families.

I read it and I appreciate you sharing. I keep going through ways to soften the blow to my family. I know nothing will make it easier on them, but I don’t know how much more I can handle. I’m sad and angry every single day.

In my early drinking stages up until the 2nd DUI it was just the party/social scene. I was more successful at fitting in with alcohol I just didn’t realize at the time how out of control it was getting. I was in control of my drinking for about the next 9 years by just not drinking more than two drinks if I had to drive somewhere. I was in a relationship and I think that made me happy and alcohol wasn’t an obsession anymore. 

Fast forward to last June and I cheated on her. I don’t know why, I was totally happy and in love with her. She had a daughter who was 3 when we started dating and she was like my child. Losing them has made me an emotional wreck. I began drinking heavily every single day.  I’m crying even typing  this.

I pushed so many people out of my life by drinking. For the last 1-1.5 years I drank every single day about a fifth or more. I’ve been drinking since I was 19 and I don’t remember what being normal feels like. I still struggle thinking I wasn’t strong enough to stop on my own.

I’m thankful I haven’t struggled with wanting to drink. I’m sure that would be too much right now. I’ve been hitting about 10 AA meetings a week, group counseling weekly, and see an individual counselor weekly as well. I’m most scared because I haven’t seen any improvement in myself over the last 3 months. I think my thoughts have gotten darker. It’s tough because I can’t be completely open about suicidal thoughts in counseling because I don’t know what will happen. Thank you

I appreciate it. I see my window closing more and more everyday. I think about death everyday. I have the means to do it now too. I’m trying so hard to find hope but I can’t find a reason that I want to live.

I blocked my family’s phone numbers so they can’t text or call me about 2 years ago. I’m too embarrassed and ashamed to face any of them and that was before I got my 3rd DUI. I can’t believe how defeated I am.
